default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-368.title: Low-energy break-bar fade
E-368.hypothesis: A close through the recent high/low printed by a bar whose range is small for its minute of day means the level gave way to a trickle of orders, not to an initiative burst; nobody with size is behind it, so liquidity providers lean on it and price returns into the box; fade the break.

E-369.title: Value-interior micro-break fade
E-369.hypothesis: While the close is within k volume-weighted standard deviations of today's volume-weighted mean, price is still inside the session's accepted value, where responsive traders on both sides are active; a short-term break there is rotation inside value rather than initiative, so fade it.

E-370.title: Clock-mark range-position fade on balanced days
E-370.hypothesis: At each :00/:30 mark desks and slicers reassess; on a day whose move from the open is not larger than usual for the minute, a close near the top (bottom) of the day's range at the mark is where the day's responsive sellers (buyers) rest, so lean against the range position toward the middle.

E-371.title: Opening-price rotation regime micro-break fade
E-371.hypothesis: When price has crossed the session open several times in the last two hours, the day traders' zero line is being contested and neither side holds inventory; short-term breaks in that regime are pushed by stops and rotate back, so fade them only while the open keeps being crossed.

E-372.title: Deep inside yesterday's range micro-break fade
E-372.hypothesis: Far from both of yesterday's extremes (more than k typical 30-minute moves from each), no reference level or stop pool is nearby to pull price; a short-term break there has nothing to run to and is absorbed by traders working inside yesterday's accepted range, so fade it.

E-373.title: Narrow box inside a wide day break fade
E-373.hypothesis: A recent box that is only a small share of the day's already wide range is a pause inside a market whose real edges are far away; its break triggers only local stops, while the day's larger participants trade the wider edges, so the break reverts into the box.

E-374.title: Break away from the prior close when already stretched
E-374.hypothesis: Yesterday's settlement-close is the overnight inventory's reference; when price is already more than k typical hourly moves away from it, a further short-term break away is chased by late momentum traders while holders of the overnight inventory take profit, so fade the break back toward the prior close.

E-375.title: Wide initial-balance interior micro-break fade
E-375.hypothesis: A first hour (or half hour) whose range already covers most of a typical day's range-to-date has set broad value early, with longer-timeframe traders active at both edges; later short-term breaks that stay inside that initial balance are noise between the edges and revert, so fade them.

E-376.title: Choppy-dollar index micro-break fade
E-376.hypothesis: Macro and foreign flow moves the dollar with direction; when the dollar's last 30 minutes have been a path with little net progress (low efficiency), no macro flow is driving Brazil assets, so a WIN short-term break is local flow that market makers fade back into the box.

E-377.title: Top-third exit rotation follow
E-377.hypothesis: After price has stayed in the top third of the day's (normal-or-wider) range for a while, the first close back below it shows the buyers who held it there have stopped defending; their exits and the responsive sellers rotate price toward the middle of the range, so sell the exit (mirror from the bottom third).
